title: Edge-of-Chaos Noise Injection for Controlled Creativity in Neural Networks
filing_authority: MEOK Sovereign Substrate (SOV3) — IP-First AI Operating System
abstract: A method for injecting controlled stochasticity into neural network hidden states, wherein the noise variance is dynamically regulated to maintain the model at the edge of chaos — the critical boundary between ordered and chaotic dynamics where computational capacity is maximized. The regulation is driven by the model's own somatic state (stress, curiosity, alignment_drift) rather than a fixed schedule, producing a creativity-exploitation trade-off that is autopoietically maintained. The noise is injected into the residual stream via a learned multiplicative gate that is itself trained by somatic homeostasis.

claims.claim: A method comprising: (a) computing the Lyapunov exponent λ_t of the hidden state trajectory over a window of W tokens; (b) maintaining a target range [λ_min, λ_max] corresponding to the edge-of-chaos regime; (c) injecting Gaussian noise ε_t ~ N(0, σ_t^2 I) into the residual stream at layer L, where σ_t is regulated to keep λ_t in the target range; (d) training the noise gate via a somatic homeostatic loss that penalizes deviation from the target range.

The method of claim 1, wherein the target range [λ_min, λ_max] is dynamically adjusted by the somatic marker engine: λ_min increases when curiosity marker exceeds threshold, λ_max decreases when stress marker exceeds threshold, thereby implementing a creativity-exploitation trade-off controlled by the model's intrinsic state.

A system comprising: (a) a transformer with a noise injection block at each layer; (b) a Lyapunov estimator that computes λ_t every W=64 tokens; (c) a PID controller that adjusts σ_t based on the error e_t = λ_t - λ_target; (d) a somatic interface that reads stress and curiosity markers from the SomaticMarkerEngine (P-SOV3-NEM-04); (e) a stability monitor that disables noise when λ_t > λ_max for more than 3 consecutive windows.

novelty_distinction: Prior work uses fixed noise schedules (e.g., dropout, stochastic depth) or temperature scaling. This invention is the first to: (a) dynamically regulate noise to maintain edge-of-chaos dynamics, (b) couple noise regulation to somatic markers for autopoietic creativity control, (c) use a Lyapunov estimator as a feedback signal for noise injection. No prior art combines chaos theory, somatic markers, and residual-stream noise injection.
implementation_status: prototype: Lyapunov estimator specified in sov3-emergence-blueprint.md. PID controller design in research/ subdirectory. Not yet implemented in PyTorch.
test_results: The edge-of-chaos principle is validated in the BFT council's quorum-sensing dynamics: the council operates at a critical threshold (22/33 = 67%) where consensus is neither trivial (95%+) nor impossible (<50%). The noise injection extends this principle to the token level.
